newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada July trade surplus falls to C$3.07 bln.
newsitem.headline: Canada July trade surplus falls to C$3.07 bln.

text.p: Canada's merchandise trade surplus fell in July to C$3.07 billion from C$3.21 billion in June (revised from C$3.14 billion), Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
Note: Figures in billions of current Canadian dollars, on a balance of payments basis, seasonally adjusted.
Statistics Canada said July exports reached a record high.

Statistics Canada said the record exports came from a surge in lumber shipments to the United States, as well as strong exports of auto parts. Grain sales remained sluggish in July, the agency said. Exports to the United States and Japan were higher, but shipments to all other trading partners declined.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$3.2 billion in July. The survey also forecast imports of C$19.1 billion and exports of C$22.3 billion in July.

Statistics Canada said imports grew by 3.2 percent in July, the second monthly increase in a row. July's level was the highest since February. The largest increase came from the industrial goods and machinery sectors.
